title: How to build a B2B prospect list: Steps, template and example
summary: Learn how to build a prospect list. Use a B2B template to check company fit, verify contacts, and remove duplicates.
body_markdown:
Building a B2B prospect list starts with one target segment. Find companies that meet its requirements, then identify the people responsible for the work your offer addresses. Check their current details and remove duplicate or unsuitable records before handing the list to sales.


Use the template below to record your findings. The worked example shows how to handle duplicate rows, contacts who have changed jobs, and accounts that need more research.


## What is a prospect list?


A prospect list records potential customers your team may contact. In B2B sales, it connects companies with relevant people and explains why each account belongs on the list.


An account is the company you might sell to; a contact is a person there who may own or influence the relevant work. Keep these records separate, with a way to link several contacts to the same account.


Being on the list does not make a company a qualified opportunity. You may have evidence that the business fits your market without knowing whether it has an active need or plans to buy.


## Copy this prospect list template


Give each contact a row in your spreadsheet and link people at the same business through a company domain or account ID. If you find a suitable company before identifying a contact, mark its account record for research.


Use the fields below as column headings, leaving out optional details that have no bearing on your campaign.


### Company information


Field What to record


Company and account ID Company name, website domain, or an existing CRM account ID


Reason for fit How the business meets your campaign’s company criteria


Supporting source Links supporting the fit assessment, with the date checked


Missing information Any essential company requirement you have not confirmed


Account owner or existing relationship Who manages the account and whether it is already a customer or active opportunity


### Contact and review information


Field What to record


Contact name and role Current employer, job title, and connection to the work you want to discuss


Role source Where you checked the person’s current role and when


Contact method The work email or other contact route needed for your campaign


Verification status Check result, method or provider, and check date; retain uncertain results


Contact restrictions Any existing do-not-contact or suppression status


Record decision Research further, review for outreach, merge duplicate, or exclude from this campaign


Next action and owner What needs to happen next and who will do it


When sources disagree, note the conflict so the next person can see why a field remains unresolved.


## How to build a prospect list, step by step


### 1. Choose one target segment


Choose a campaign segment from your ideal customer profile. Specify the company requirements and the roles you want to reach before searching.


You might focus on one type of business in a market you serve, with a workflow your product supports. Decide which requirements are essential and which are preferences. A preferred company size should not override a confirmed product limitation.


Also list exclusions, such as unsupported use cases or accounts already managed through another sales process.


### 2. Find sources that match the segment


Company websites can help you check services and markets served. Directories and event pages can help you discover businesses to investigate. Choose each source for the information it can support.


Source Useful for What to check next


Company websites Services, markets served, team information, and product details Whether the page supports the specific requirement you are checking


Industry directories and association lists Finding companies in a particular sector Current activity and fit on the company’s own website


Event exhibitor or speaker pages Discovering companies connected with a topic or event The company’s role in the event and relevance to your offer


Existing relationships and CRM records Referrals, previously researched accounts, and earlier conversations Current ownership, relationship status, and whether details have changed


Company and contact research tools Searching for accounts and adding available contact information Evidence behind the match and any missing or conflicting details


Treat an event listing or directory category as a lead for research. Check the company against your requirements before adding it to the campaign. Neither source alone establishes full company fit or a buying project.


### 3. Check company fit before researching every contact


For each company, work through your essential requirements and save the evidence behind your decision, including the date checked.


Assign a research task when an essential fact is missing. If your product requires a particular system, for example, an empty technology field leaves that requirement unresolved. It does not prove that the company uses an incompatible system.


A confirmed mismatch is a reason to stop researching that account for this campaign. Finding more contacts will not resolve a product limitation.


Our[B2B prospect research guide](https://blog.floworks.ai/how-to-research-a-b2b-prospect-before-outreach/) explains how to check companies and prepare useful research notes.


### 4. Identify people connected to the work


Find the department or function responsible for the problem your offer addresses. Before adding a person to the campaign, check their current employer and responsibilities.


A senior title can help you identify a possible contact, but it does not establish purchasing authority. A department leader and an operations manager may both be relevant for different reasons.


If both people are relevant, give each a row linked to the same account. That lets the team coordinate contact instead of sending overlapping messages independently.


### 5. Add the contact details your campaign needs


For an email campaign, record the work address and its verification result alongside the check date and provider or method used. Retain uncertain results so someone can follow up on them.


Before using an address that passes a check, confirm that the record has the correct person and company attached. Conflicting role information or an uncertain address needs further research.


Add phone details when your workflow calls for them, since extra fields also need maintenance.


### 6. Review duplicates and existing records


Check whether your existing account and contact records already contain the companies or people you have found.


For companies, check domains or account IDs alongside names. Review related brands or subsidiaries before merging them. For people, compare the available identifiers, including the work address and profile URL. Resolve conflicting details before treating two records as the same person.


A shared employer does not make two people duplicates. If the same person appears in two exports, compare the records and merge them once you confirm the match. Preserve useful source notes and the current owner.


Also check customer accounts, active opportunities, recent contact history, and suppression records. Those checks determine whether an account belongs in this campaign or needs coordination with someone else.


### 7. Assign a decision and next action


Decision When to use it


Research further An essential fit detail, current role, or contact route remains unresolved


Review for outreach The record meets your documented list criteria and can move to campaign review


Merge duplicate You have confirmed that records describe the same contact or account


Exclude from this campaign A confirmed mismatch, contact restriction, or campaign exclusion applies


Pass the evidence and verification notes to the salesperson with the record, so they can understand why it was selected without repeating the research.


“Review for outreach” is a list-management decision. The campaign still needs a suitable message and sending checks. Our[B2B sales outreach checklist](https://blog.floworks.ai/b2b-sales-outreach-checklist/) covers that next stage.


## A worked B2B prospect list example


Suppose a fictional company sells software for collecting and tracking client approvals. Its campaign targets US marketing agencies that manage recurring client campaigns. Relevant contacts work in client services or operations.


All companies, people, source notes, and check results below are fictional. The domains use .example and are placeholders, not real prospect websites.


Record What the research shows Decision and next action


Juniper Creative, juniper.example: Avery Chen, Head of Client Services Company pages support the agency and recurring-campaign criteria. A current team page confirms Avery’s role. The work address has a recorded passing check. Review for outreach after checking account history and contact restrictions


Juniper Creative: Sam Patel, Operations Manager Same company, different person with relevant responsibilities. Current role evidence is recorded, but the work address is unresolved. Keep as a separate contact; research the contact route and coordinate with Juniper’s account owner


Juniper Creative: Avery Chen, second imported row The profile URL and work address match Avery’s existing record. This row adds a useful source note. Merge the confirmed duplicate and preserve the additional note


Harbor Studio, harbor.example: contact not yet selected The company is a US marketing agency. Available pages do not establish whether it manages recurring client campaigns. Research the missing company requirement before adding contacts


Maple Campaigns, maple.example: Jordan Lee An older directory lists Jordan as Operations Director. A current profile shows a different employer. Remove Jordan from this account’s campaign list and research the current role holder


Ridge Events, ridge.example: contact not yet selected The company’s services confirm event production outside this campaign’s defined market. Exclude from this campaign


Merging Avery’s duplicate leaves two distinct contacts at Juniper Creative. Sam still needs a usable contact route. Harbor needs company research, while Maple needs a current contact.


Even Avery’s completed record does not establish an active approval problem or an intention to buy. Those remain questions for a conversation.


## How to check list quality and keep it current


Review the list as if you were the salesperson receiving it. The sources should explain company fit and support the contact’s current role. Mark uncertain fields clearly and name the person responsible for resolving them.


Look for missing sources, outdated roles, unresolved duplicates, and unexplained fit decisions, even in rows where every cell is filled.


Keep records needing research separate from those moving to outreach review. Before expanding the search, review a sample and investigate whether recurring errors come from the source or your search criteria.


Recheck current roles and contact details before use, along with any recent event you plan to mention. If a buyer corrects a detail or the team finds that an account is unsuitable, update the record and keep the source or explanation with the correction.

## Frequently asked questions


### How do you build a B2B prospect list from scratch?


Define one target segment and the company requirements it must meet. Find matching businesses, record evidence of fit, and identify current contacts in relevant roles. Check their contact details and existing account records, then assign a next action to each row.


### Can you build a prospect list without paid tools?


Yes. Research companies through public websites, directories, and event pages, then organize the findings in a spreadsheet. Check current roles and the contact route you intend to use. When considering a tool, compare that research effort with the work it would help you do.


### How can you build a prospect list faster?


Work on a narrow segment with a consistent set of fields, and test your sources on a small batch before collecting more records. Check company fit before searching for contacts and compare new records with existing data. Tools can help with discovery and enrichment. Assign unresolved research tasks to an owner so the team knows who will finish them.
